title: Experiment Lab: Visual Runbook for Multi-dimensional Rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and prototype an ‘Experiment Lab’ UI that lets product and platform engineers create, preview, and evaluate multi-dimensional rollouts (canary + feature flags + weighted A/B + region splits) in a single, composable workspace. The goal is a low-friction visual runbook where teams can: define traffic slices across axes (model variant, region, capacity tier), attach evaluation metrics and automated safety checks, preview request flows with synthetic or replayed traces, and stage quick rollback actions. This is a different approach from linear traffic editors: the Experiment Lab emphasizes pre-flight simulation, hypothesis-driven experiment scaffolding, and an easily shareable runbook artifact for post-mortems.
updates: 2025-02-16: Kickoff workshop with PM and Eng. Aligned on scope: focus on mid-complexity rollouts (up to 3 axes) for beta customers.
2025-02-20: First wireframe session. Explored lane-based timeline vs node-graph. Chose a hybrid: timeline for time-based ramps + node panel for axis definitions.
2025-02-25: Usability testing with 6 engineers (internal). Key findings: users want a compact preview that shows both traffic split percentages and sample request routing examples.
2025-02-28: Design review with Security and SRE. SRE requested explicit fallback policy configuration and a lightweight mode for Dedicated seats.
2025-03-02: Iteration completed on Figma. Preparing handoff artifacts and proposals for ENG-10014 API surface for simulation endpoints. Submitted PRD link in attachments.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Prototype allows defining up to 3 rollout axes and persisting them as a sharable runbook.
A2: Simulation mode can replay sampled traces and surface per-metric impact overlays (latency, cost per token, error rate) in the prototype.
A3: Users can create a staged rollback plan (automatic trigger thresholds + manual rollback button) in the UI.
A4: Handoff package includes component specs, interaction patterns, and a minimal API contract for ENG to implement simulations.
mock_user_feedback: "I like being able to see a sample of requests routed to each variant — it made it much easier to reason about data skew." - internal BE engineer
"We need a quick-summary card for executives that hides technical axis details but shows risk and expected cost delta." - PM
"Fallback settings must default to safe behavior for Dedicated customers; make them visible in the top-level runbook header." - SRE
decision_log: Chose hybrid timeline + node panel approach over pure node-graph to reduce learning curve for existing users.
Simulation will be opt-in and use sampled traces to avoid throughput impact on production systems.
Will surface cost delta estimates using Optimize heuristics; ENG to provide API endpoint in ENG-10067.
